title: Claim Record and the RentGuard Reinstatement Fee
content:
The reinstatement fee on a RentGuard Renters Policy carries an addition for the policy's claim record over the last 36 calendar months.

## The rule

- When a renters claim payment was issued on the policy in the last 36 calendar months, 5.00 is added to the fee.
- When a renters claim was reported in the last 36 calendar months but no claim payment was issued in that period, 2.00 is added.
- When no renters claim was reported in the last 36 calendar months, nothing is added.

## Questions answered

**Which records count?** The policy's claim file entries: a claim payment is an entry recording claim money issued, dated when issued; a reported claim is an entry recording first notice of loss, dated when reported. Each counts when its date falls within the last 36 calendar months.

**A claim was reported 40 months ago and paid 30 months ago. What is added?** 5.00, because a renters claim payment was issued in the last 36 calendar months.

**A claim was reported 10 months ago and nothing has been paid. What is added?** 2.00, because a claim was reported in the last 36 calendar months and no claim payment was issued in that period.

**The only claim was reported and paid 38 months ago. What is added?** Nothing, because no renters claim was reported in the last 36 calendar months and no claim payment was issued in that period.

| Claim payment issued in the last 36 calendar months | Claim reported in the last 36 calendar months | Added to the fee |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes or no | 5.00 |
| no | yes | 2.00 |
| no | no | nothing |

The claims and dates in the questions above are hypothetical.
